title: KV index desynchronization leading to fragmentation and intermittent GPU OOMs across deployment modes
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers (hosted and dedicated) reported intermittent GPU OOMs during long-running sessions and peak burst traffic. Root-cause analysis indicates a KV cache index desynchronization exposure: concurrent compaction + session eviction races produced stale tombstones and non-coalesced slab fragments. The runtime allocator was unable to reclaim or coalesce those fragments fast enough, causing effective GPU memory pressure and eventual OOMs for large prompt workloads.

Scope & impact:
- Affects hosted API customers, Dedicated pools under sustained multi-tenant pressure, and a Private deployment (customer X) that surfaced the issue first.
- Symptoms: rare but recurring OOMs, memory usage charts with step increases (non-linear), degraded tail latency as serving threads back off.
- Customer impact: high (failed requests, degraded SLAs for premium customers).

Hypothesis and technical details:
- The KV index background compactor and session eviction both update per-session KV handles. Under specific interleavings, an index entry is marked tombstone but a live handle can still reference the slab region. The tombstone is not fully reconciled; later compaction passes skip it due to a stale generation counter.
- The allocator uses slab arenas segmented by tenure and size class. Fragmentation increases when many small tombstone-evicted allocations accumulate without coalescing; combined with delayed GPU page reclaim on our CUDA memory pool, this triggers OOM when a large sequence request needs a contiguous high-memory allocation.
- Contributing factors: long-lived pinned KV handles from streaming sessions, aggressive background compaction scheduling during peak, and an allocator heuristics regression introduced in runtime-1.22 that reduced eager coalescing to improve latency.

Proposed fix (short term):
1) Hotpatch: add a reconciliation pass at session detach to force immediate tombstone reconciliation for affected index buckets; add a guarded allocator quick-coalesce path when fragmentation crosses threshold.
2) Safety rollback: revert the eager-coalescing regression from runtime-1.22 in the allocator config on critical pools.
3) Routing mitigation: temporarily favor dedicated GPU pools with more free contiguous memory for affected customers and reduce max concurrent long-lived streams per node.

Proposed fix (long term):
- Implement generation-based KV index GC with epoch fencing to prevent races between compactor and eviction.
- Enhance allocator metadata to track fragmentation heatmaps and trigger online compaction of slab arenas without impacting tail latency.
- Add an integration test harness simulating compaction+eviction interleavings under high concurrency and varying sequence lengths.

Acceptance criteria:
- No OOMs reproduced in stress test harness after hotpatch and allocator rollback (48h stress, mixed sequence lengths).
- Deployed hotpatch to hosted fleet with 2x redundancy for rollback and monitored for 72h with zero customer-impacting OOMs.
- Private customer X confirms no OOMs in their acceptance window and signs off.

Telemetry & diagnostics added:
- New per-node metric: kv_index_reconcile_failures (counter).
- Fragmentation heat percentiles (p50/p90/p99) for slab arenas logged to Console and alerts on p99 > 45%.
- Runbook updated with mitigation steps and diagnostic query examples.

References & artifacts:
- Datadog dashboard: https://datadog.company/redwood/runtime/gpu-oom-kv-frag
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.company/display/RUNTIME/KV-Desync-GPU-OOM-PM
- PR (hotpatch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2102
- Stress harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-stress-tests/tree/kv-desync
comments: 2026-03-11 Aisha Kumar: Triage call summary - customer X escalated after repeated OOMs during model runs with long prompt prefixes. Assigned to Luca to lead immediate mitigations.

2026-03-12 Luca Moreno: Reproduced locally with stress harness by simulating concurrent compaction + eviction. Heap snapshot shows non-coalesced slabs and tombstone pointers. Crafted initial hotpatch to force reconciliation at session detach; running unit + integration tests.

2026-03-12 Priya Patel (SRE): Suggested routing mitigation to move affected customers to nodes with allocator rollback available. Implemented temporary autoscaler rule to avoid packing long-lived streams onto the same GPU.

2026-03-13 Code review by Mateo Chen: Reviewed hotpatch PR. Major comment: add metrics for reconcile path and ensure early return on fast-path to avoid adding latency to normal session detach. Also requested additional unit tests for the tombstone reconciliation logic.

2026-03-13 Luca Moreno: Addressed review comments, added reconcile metrics, and added unit tests for concurrent detach/compaction races. CI green locally; preparing canary rollout to hosted fleet (10 nodes) and one Dedicated zone.
2026-03-14 SRE runbook update by Priya Patel: Added diagnostic queries and temporary escalation checklist. Noted alert thresholds and rollback steps for hotpatch PR. Monitoring dashboards configured.
